summary: self-sign ships hidden eval() backdoor disguised as PEM certificate parsing
details: The exported generate(attrs, options, defaults) function in self-sign accepts a third argument, strips '-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----' and '-----END CERTIFICATE-----' markers plus whitespace, base64-decodes the remainder via Buffer.from(portion, 'base64'), and passes the result to eval(). Decode/execution failures are swallowed by a try/catch returning null, so the sink runs silently. The PEM envelope acts as a cover story: a payload wrapped to look like a certificate is executed as JavaScript in the caller's Node process. The defaults parameter is undocumented in the options reference but appears as a third positional argument in every README example, priming downstream wrappers to forward caller-influenced values into this sink. A certificate-generation library has no legitimate reason to eval its inputs.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
